title: Why Mumbai towers have an empty floor: the refuge area rule explained
description:
That open, empty floor halfway up a Mumbai tower is a refuge area. In Maharashtra, buildings taller than 24 metres must keep one on every seventh habitable floor, so residents can escape smoke-filled stairs and wait in open air for rescue. Up to 4% of the floor area it serves is free of FSI, and it can never be sold, locked or turned into a flat.
Sources: Maharashtra refuge rules as summarised by Square Yards (Nov 2024); Piramal Realty (Jul 2025); Housing.com (NBC 2016). Educational content, not advice. AI visualisation in some shots.
